collection.title: Emerging transient dynamics at finite observation scales
collection.authors: Cobo-Lopez, S.; Carbajal, L. J.; Witt, M.; Rohwer, F. L.; Luque, A.
collection.abstract: Biogeochemical, ecological, and astronomical systems are transient. Yet, predicting dynamical shifts remains challenging because of inferential uncertainties in datasets and the limitations of asymptotic-dependent theories. To address this problem, we developed a theoretical framework that builds on the finite nature of observations. This framework assesses the relative importance of processes, defined as the mechanisms that contribute to the rate of change of the system's dynamic variables; this allows prediction of switching thresholds, that is, the values of the dynamic variables at which a process becomes relevant or irrelevant, switching the dynamics into a new dynamic regime. The framework predicts that the number of possible observable dynamic regimes increases exponentially with the number of processes. Yet observers are expected to experience only a subset of those dynamic regimes, determined by which processes remain relevant throughout the observation. The framework was tested on a case study of a classic predator-prey system comprising four processes parameterized for bacteria (prey) and lytic bacteriophages (predator). The analysis recovered the sixteen dynamic regimes predicted by the framework, including two non-trivial quasi-equilibrium dynamics. The classical quasi-equilibrium solution, with all processes being relevant, was observed in only about one in ten simulated trajectories that covered the observational window. An adaptive Boolean model, using only relevant observable processes, validated the framework's accuracy by recovering the full model's dynamics within the observer's tolerance. The observational framework introduced here provides a strategy for identifying the processes and conditions that lead to significant switches in dynamic regimes. The framework complements asymptotic approaches to transient dynamics by focusing on the observer's specific, finite context rather than the system's asymptotic states. It can also guide experimental design to measure a process's impact in a dynamical system and suggests actions to suppress it.

collection.title: Long-term Epstein-Barr virus persistence in immunocompetent, primate-related Chinese tree shrews and inducible lytic reactivation in species-matched epithelial cultures
collection.authors: Avilala, J.; Dochi, H.; Wekselblatt, J.; Flemington, E.; Pierce, A.; Brown, C.; Dobek, G.; Ott, K.; Roussel, P.; Abdelghani, R.; Becnel, D.; Sides, M.; Morris, G. F.; Liu, H.; Feng, W.; Lin, Z.
collection.abstract: Experimental models combining long-term Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection in immunocompetent animals with species-matched cellular systems for studying viral regulation remain limited. Chinese tree shrews combine evolutionary proximity to primates with small-animal practicality and native immunocompetence, offering a complementary nonrodent model. We serially monitored blood and oral specimens from six animals inoculated with Akata EBV. Five were followed for approximately two years, including two beyond two years, and the sixth underwent tissue collection at approximately six months. Intermittent EBV DNA detection included blood positivity beyond two years in one animal. Viral RNA localized to liver, lung, and spleen at six months and to liver and spleen of another animal near two years, supporting persistent infection. All tested blood and oral specimens from six uninoculated controls were negative. In parallel, renewable lung-derived epithelial/mesothelial-like cultures maintained EBV infection in two immortalization backgrounds. Viral profiling identified Qp-associated EBNA1 transcription and latency-associated expression alongside spontaneous lytic transcription. Host transcriptomics identified 684 robust EBV-associated expression changes, with prominent enrichment of MYC and E2F target programs and metabolic pathways, together with reduced interferon- and inflammatory-response transcription across both backgrounds. These findings nominate MYC/E2F-associated host programs as candidate regulators of the balance between maintained infection and lytic activity. Zta expression and sodium butyrate induced lytic reactivation, with infectious virus production demonstrated after sodium butyrate treatment. This integrated platform complements humanized mice and nonhuman-primate models and connects long-term EBV persistence in vivo with experimentally accessible studies of host regulation and the latent-to-lytic transition in species-matched cultures.

collection.title: The key role of oxidation state and flake size in the ecotoxicological impact of industrial graphene oxide nanoflakes
collection.authors: Subrati, A.; Bigini, P.; De Luigi, A.; Natale, C.; Mehennaoui, K.; Houin, M.; Chary, A.; Serchi, T.; Venus, T.; Saorin, A.; Monopoli, M. P.; Zhang, X.; Zhao, K.; Alonso, B.; Estrela-Lopis, I.; Gao, C.; Zabeo, A.; Hristozov, D.; Moya, S.; Diomede, L.
collection.author_corresponding_institution: istituto di Ricerche farmacologiche Mario Negri
collection.abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) is a widely used nanomaterial across various scientific and technological fields. Environmental exposure to GO and consequent ecotoxicological effects have been largely reported. Despite the significant efforts and illuminating conclusions, establishing fair pairwise correlations between material and toxicity descriptors remains challenging and controversial. Key drawbacks in GO ecotoxicological studies to date include a lack of standardized materials, poorly defined descriptors, and insufficient material variants. Here, we establish the first comprehensive framework to tackle the multidimensional ecotoxicology of GO. We perform thorough material characterization to derive descriptors that precisely define four key GO variants used in industrial scale-up, with differing flake granularity and oxidation extent. These GO variants are evaluated against toxicological endpoint descriptors across two animal models (Daphnia magna and Caenorhabditis elegans) and two plant models (rice and pepper). Our findings underscore the inherently multidimensional nature of GO toxicity by identifying key physicochemical properties associated with it. This study provides an unprecedented platform for parametrizing GO materials using material and toxicity descriptors to contribute to nanomaterial safety.
